nws.title: Weather Service watches and warnings
nws.detail: Nothing for Western New York right now.

ao.title: Arctic Oscillation: is cold air escaping?
ao.detail: Model average goes as low as -1.6 (Nov 3) and as high as +1.3. Below -2 = cold air can escape south. Above +2.5 = cold stays up north.

nao.title: North Atlantic Oscillation: is cold air steered our way?
nao.detail: Model average goes as low as -0.6 (Nov 12) and as high as +1.0. Below -1.5 = cold air gets steered into the East.

cpc610.title: NOAA 6–10 day outlook for Buffalo
cpc610.detail: Nov 3–Nov 7: 70% chance of being warmer than normal.

cpc814.title: NOAA 8–14 day outlook for Buffalo
cpc814.detail: Nov 5–Nov 11: 50% chance of being warmer than normal.

erie.title: Lake Erie water temperature
erie.detail: Oct 27: 4°F warmer than normal (57°F). Record for the date: 61.9°F (2017). Warmer water = more fuel for lake-effect snow.

vortex.title: Will the polar vortex break down?
vortex.detail: In 21 of 31 runs of the American weather model, the spinning winds over the Arctic stop and reverse within 34 days, as early as Nov 4. That can send Arctic air south 1 to 3 weeks later. Yesterday: 65%.

noreaster.title: Nor'easter in the next 10 days?
noreaster.detail: 1 of 31 model runs show a strong storm off the Northeast coast around Nov 6. Strongest run: 988 mb (lower = stronger).

freeze.title: First freeze in Buffalo
freeze.detail: Not yet this fall. 1 of 31 model runs freeze within 10 days, around Nov 7. Coldest run: 31°F.

arctic.title: Arctic air over Buffalo?
arctic.detail: 0 of 31 model runs bring air colder than 14°F about 5,000 ft up in the next 10 days. Coldest run: 18°F up there.

lakeeffect.title: Lake-effect snow setup?
lakeeffect.detail: 5 of 31 model runs get cold enough over Lake Erie (62°F water) for lake-effect snow around Nov 7. 100% show lake-effect rain showers.

seiche.title: Lake Erie seiche (sloshing) now
seiche.detail: Buffalo water level minus Toledo: -0.3 ft (Buffalo 2.1 ft above low water). 6+ ft difference = a big seiche.

waves.title: Lake Erie waves now
waves.detail: Eastern Lake Erie buoy: 0.7 ft waves. 8+ ft = big wave day.

aurora.title: Northern lights in the next 3 days?
aurora.detail: Highest forecast: Kp 5.0 around Oct 31. Kp 6+ = maybe visible from WNY, 7+ = good chance.

storms.title: Thunderstorm photo days
storms.detail: No thunderstorms expected in the next 3 days.

seichewind.title: Seiche / big-wave wind coming?
seichewind.detail: 0 of 31 model runs blow SW winds of 35+ mph down Lake Erie in the next 10 days. Strongest run: 34 mph.

seasmoke.title: Sea smoke (lake steam) mornings
seasmoke.detail: Needs Buffalo at 32°F or colder over 62°F water. 1 of 31 model runs get there around Nov 7.

fallsice.title: Niagara Falls ice?
fallsice.detail: 0 of 31 model runs bring 3 straight nights at 10°F or colder in the next 10 days.

recent.text: 🗺️ NOAA's forecast for Nov 3–Nov 7 got more confident: Buffalo now has a 70% chance of being warmer than normal (before: 60% chance warmer than normal). This comes from NOAA's Climate Prediction Center, which forecasts whether the weeks ahead will run warmer or colder than usual.

🌊 Lake Erie is unusually warm for Oct 26: 61.9°F, about 4°F warmer than normal. The record for this date is 62.1°F (2017). Warm lake water is fuel for lake-effect snow: when cold air blows over it, the lake adds heat and moisture, which can build heavier snow bands.

🌪️ The polar vortex may break down. The polar vortex is a huge spinning wind high above the Arctic that usually keeps the coldest air locked up north. In 20 of 31 runs of the American weather model (65%), that spin stops and reverses, as early as Nov 4. When that happens, Arctic air often spills south 1 to 3 weeks later, which can mean cold and snow for Buffalo. Yesterday it was 35%.
